correctness.rationale: For the confluent or distinct two-node Szegő span, the finite Blaschke product B(z)=(z²-sz+p)/(1-conj(s)z+conj(p)z²) has model space V=H²⊖B H², so the orthogonal error of z² equals the sum of the squared moduli of its first three Taylor coefficients. Those are c0=p, c1=t=-s+p conj(s), c2=1-|p|²+conj(s)t. Setting x=|p|, y=|t| and A=1-x², Schwarz–Pick supplies 0<=y<=A. Inverting t to solve s=-(t+p conj(t))/A and bounding c2 gives error² >= x²+(1-x)u+(A-u)² with u=y²/(1-x). Completing squares gives 9/16+((2x-1)²(4x+3))/16+[u-(1-x)(x+1/2)]², valid for every pair including repeated nodes. Equality forces x=1/2,u=1/2, |t|=1/2 and phase alignment; after a common rotation the zeros are exactly (1±i)/2. That pair has c0=1/2,c1=-1/2,c2=1/4 and error²=9/16, giving captured energy 7/16. Independently verified the polynomial sum-of-squares identity exactly in SymPy and the 2×2 complex kernel Gram projection numerically to high precision. These finite calculations are checks, not the global proof.
scope: Classical H²(D), f(z)=z², two arbitrary complex Szegő kernel nodes (or confluent node derivative); probability-normalized Hardy coefficient inner product.
